absent: Backing width and position of table selector and identifier fields and feature register values beyond observed masking.
Setup of stolen time base address and scheduling delay source beyond observed delta accumulation.
Full system register descriptor table, sanitised range bounds, and per register reset effects.
Interrupt target selection policy and full LPI allocation and release lifecycle.
Low level guest entry helper, exit handler table contents, and fault decode and condition helpers.
Timer reset and synchronization effects and userspace interrupt controller interaction details.

findings.text: Exposes a helper that returns the address space identifier for a vCPU for either of two translation regimes. It reads the matching translation control register, uses its table selector bit to choose between the two table base registers of that regime, extracts the identifier field, and keeps only the low portion unless sixteen bit identifiers are both supported and enabled.
Passing a regime other than the two supported values triggers a fatal abort rather than returning a value.
The nested control address reader returns the stored control value widened by forty eight bit sign extension.
Provides a reload operation for vCPU performance monitor state that narrows three control masks to the implemented set and delegates reprogramming of that set.
The implemented counter set always contains the cycle counter plus a low run of event counters derived from the configured counter count, with zero count meaning cycle only.

Reprogramming walks the architected maximum counter range, skips counters outside the supplied mask, enables backing tracking where the counter is enabled and disables otherwise, then restores guest monitor state. An empty mask returns without walking.

Enabling a monitor counter creates its backing host event when absent and otherwise enables it with a debug report on failure to reach active state. Disabling only acts when a backing event exists and otherwise does nothing.

Stolen time accounting is skipped when the guest area address is marked invalid. Otherwise it reads the guest stolen field under shared protection, converts endianness, adds the delta of host scheduling delay since the last update, and writes the result back with matching conversion.
Stolen time guest access holds the virtual machine shared read section across the read modify write of the guest field.

Reset is the vCPU reset entry that snapshots pending reset state under lock, handles transient unload and reload around the operation with preemption disabled, applies vector extension handling, resets core and system state, applies any deferred power state reset, and resets timer state.

Reset serializes the reset flag snapshot with the multiprocessor state lock and performs the unload and reload pair with preemption disabled, reloading on the current processor only if previously loaded.

Vector extension enable records the system maximum length and marks the virtual machine as having the feature with allocation deferred until finalize. Vector reset clears the saved vector state sized for the vCPU only when the vCPU has the feature.

System register reset iterates the descriptor table, skipping entries without reset handlers, dispatching feature identifier registers to virtual machine wide or per vCPU paths and all others to their own handler, refreshes sanitised entries, marks identifier registers initialized, and requests monitor reload when the vCPU has a monitor.

Feature identifier detection is based on encoding fields with fixed values for two fields and bounded ranges for the other two. Virtual machine wide identifiers are four named cache and identity registers plus a subrange of that space, and per vCPU identifiers are the remaining feature identifiers.
Register descriptors carry five encoding fields that are combined into a thirty two bit system encoding by the mapping helper.

Virtual machine wide identifier reset applies only until the initialized flag is set and otherwise leaves stored values unchanged. Per vCPU identifier reset applies only until the vCPU is marked initialized.
Asynchronous interrupt controller updates run the active list pruning with local interrupts saved and disabled to match list handling context.

Active list pruning requires interrupts disabled, holds the per vCPU list lock while examining each entry with its own lock held, and for migration drops both locks, takes a reference, then reacquires the two vCPU list locks ordered by numeric identifier with nesting annotation before revalidating.

Pruning drops entries with no target and releases their references, keeps entries already on the correct vCPU, moves entries whose target changed after revalidation and kicks the target with a pending interrupt request, restarts the walk after any migration attempt, clears the cached last list entry reference, and releases deleted entries at the end.
The debug lock check has two build variants, one that enforces the predicate as fatal and one that discards it entirely.

Thirty two bit guest mode is accepted only for thirty two bit capable vCPUs without nested virtualization when the platform supports thirty two bit at low exception level. Userspace interrupt pending state is the union of timer and monitor pending indications.
Monitor notification to userspace toggles a dedicated device level bit in the run area and reports whether notification was needed.

Pre entry exit checks first handle userspace interrupt controller pending timer or monitor changes as an interrupted entry, then fail entry on an unsupported processor with recorded reason and processor number, and otherwise report any pending vCPU request or deferred guest mode work.
Guest transition is a non instrumentable wrapper that enters guest state with interrupts off, invokes the low level run helper, then exits guest state with interrupts off and returns its status.

The run ioctl is the main vCPU execution entry. It completes pending fault emulation, verifies the vCPU wants to run, activates the signal mask, then loops over deferred work and request handling, non preemptible state flushing, guarded entry, post exit synchronization and exit dispatch until userspace handling is required, finishing with signal deactivation and consistent exception and program counter fixup.

The run loop disables preemption across nested, monitor and interrupt controller flushing, disables interrupts across controller flush and event update, publishes guest mode with an ordered store before the final exit check, and on abort restores outside mode with a barrier before synchronized re enable.

Successful entry is followed by ordered synchronization of monitor state before interrupt controller state and controller state before timer state, with additional nested timer handling for hypervisor context, a transient interrupt window for interrupt exits, early exit handling, nested synchronization, validation against forbidden thirty two bit mode, and final exit dispatch.

Floating point flush releases host ownership when thread state is marked foreign. Synchronization requires interrupts disabled and, when the guest owns the registers, binds guest register, vector and control state to the processor, selects vector versus SIMD save format by vCPU capability, and clears the foreign marker.

Exit dispatch returns to the guest for pending asynchronous errors and for interrupt and system error classes, delegates traps to trap handling, fails entry for hypervisor disappearance, fails entry with an invalid argument for illegal returns, and reports internal error for unrecognized classes.
Trap exits advance past the instruction when its condition is false and otherwise dispatch through a handler selected by the exception syndrome class field.

Early exit handling first synchronizes protected host state, then consumes pending asynchronous errors using reliability extensions when present and simple injection otherwise, and separately handles system errors from low exception level.

Protected host state tracking is inactive unless protected mode is enabled for a non protected virtual machine. Trap and error exits synchronize hypervisor state and mark host state dirty while other exits clear the marker.
Guest system error injection occurs for non reliability errors and for fatal reliability errors, while corrected reliability errors are ignored.

Fault return handling ignores already completed operations and externally aborted accesses. Reads fetch the userspace buffer with width handling, trace reporting, endian conversion, conditional sign extension and width narrowing, then store to the destination register. All completed operations advance the guest program counter and report continuation.
Run exit reasons observed include unknown, fault emulation, interrupt, fail entry and internal error, with fail entry distinguishing unsupported processor and illegal state.
The run area carries exit reason, flags, fault address and data buffer plus device level state. The vCPU carries execution mode, exit statistics, fault pending state and multiprocessor reset state.
Detecting forbidden thirty two bit mode after exit invalidates the vCPU so that further use requires explicit reinitialization, and treats the exit as illegal.
List pruning assumes the examined entry belongs to the calling vCPU and treats violation as fatal.
